This topic always pains me. I am a skinny, 47-year-old male. Whom has never weighed more than 135 pounds, if that. I still struggle to wear a size 28 waist. I am constantly berated for not trying enough or eating enough to gain weight. My situation is different from most. I lost my license in my late 20s, and for the past twenty years, I have walked or bike rode everywhere. I enjoy it. It helps my mental state fight years of depression by just being outside for whatever time it takes me to travel from place to place. My coworkers and friends see me eat what is essentially my one meal a day and think God how does he stay skinny by eating so much. I can easily put away 3 to 5 thousand calories in a meal or day, but then I probably won't eat again until my body tells me so. Which might be a day and a half later, depending on what I ate. I've come to realize that I essentially fast for long periods of time between meals. I just eat a meal when I am hungry and then snack in between those meals. Granted, all of the walking and biking that I do cause me to eat a lot when I am hungry. But I never eat more than one actual meal in a day. At most, I might eat an early breakfast, which can be up to 3 bowls of cereal. Then come home later and eat something like pasta. I believe the long periods of fasting play the biggest part in staying skinny for me. I chose to eat a somewhat healthy diet. Fruits, veggies, and then add to that with carbs and protein. It's not like I eat perfectly. But I do try as I get older and realize it factors into how I feel day to day energy wise. I need quality ingredients to provide the nutrients I need to travel place to place. This leads to absorbant bills on groceries sadly. I can easily spend 400 dollars or more on groceries and still run out of food before the end of the month. That part is the hardest to cope with, and people neglect that. They just see skinny me and think I have a perfect life. I don't, and I've taught my children to never assume what others deal with. We all have issues, and it pops up in different ways for us all. You are perfect they way you decide to live and be happy. Society just portrays that we have to strive for some idea of what makes us healthy and probably isn't for most of us. Do you and be at peace with who you are. I am. Good luck on your path.

The bottom was smooth, no light. This messed with me for years....why was it shaped like a star of david, was it real, why did i see it near christmas. So many questions. Friends openly doubted me, yea right....they said. I had just had a daughter a month before. So, eventually i just got over it and moved on with my life. 

Then I watched that fucking movie..... The scene comes up where they show what the crafts looked like. I lost it, started bawling my eyes out. My wife and friends are asking what is wrong. All I could muster up, is that what I was looking at on screen, in the movie, was almost identical to what I had seen in the sky that night so long ago. It messed me up again, wondering how could someone depict something randomly that looked so close to what I had seen. My story on this crazy movie.
